root_cause.text: The `for_each_available_child_of_node()` macro automatically calls `of_node_put()` on the child node upon loop exit, but the error handling path at the `put_child` label unconditionally calls `of_node_put()` again on the same node, resulting in a double free when `devm_request_threaded_irq()` fails.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `goto put_child;` to `return ret;` when `devm_request_threaded_irq()` fails. The CVE description explicitly states that "for_each_available_child_of_node() calls of_node_put() to release child_np in each success loop" and that after breaking from the loop, "the code will jump to the put_child label and will call the of_node_put() again," causing the double free. The fix avoids the `put_child` label entirely, preventing the second `of_node_put()` call on an already-released node.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error handling in USB2 PHY probe by returning error directly instead of jumping to cleanup label that may perform unnecessary or harmful operations.
intent_record.what: Changed the error handling path in rockchip_usb2phy_probe() from 'goto put_child;' to 'return ret;' when irq request fails.
intent_record.how: This eliminates an unnecessary jump to the put_child label when IRQ request fails. The put_child label likely performs cleanup operations (such as putting a reference to a child device), but at this point in the probe function, such cleanup may not be needed or may cause issues. The direct return skips that cleanup path and returns the error code immediately.

Author: Peter Geis <pgwipeout@gmail.com>

    phy: phy-rockchip-inno-usb2: support muxed interrupts
    
    The rk3568 usb2phy has a single muxed interrupt that handles all
    interrupts.
    Allow the driver to plug in only a single interrupt as necessary.

    Tested-by: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@wolfvision.net>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a double-free vulnerability in the error handling path. The code uses `for_each_available_child_of_node()` macro (visible in context of the probe function iterating through child nodes) which automatically calls `of_node_put()` on loop exit. However, at line 1264 in the new code, when `devm_request_threaded_irq()` fails for the muxed interrupt, the error path jumps to the `put_child:` label (line 1267) which unconditionally calls `of_node_put()` again on the same child node. This results in a double-free of the node reference. The vulnerable construct is present: the `goto put_child;` statement at line 1264 when `devm_request_threaded_irq()` fails, combined with the automatic cleanup from `for_each_available_child_of_node()` macro, causes the same node to be released twice. The fix would require either removing the manual `of_node_put()` at the label or restructuring the error handling to avoid the goto when using the for_each macro.
